v.why: When edge 0 is none, node 1 is always zero, so a conv on edge 1->3 adds nothing.
With node 1 dead, a conv on edge 1->2 has no input signal and cannot help.
If edge 2->3 is none, node 2 never reaches the output, so improving edge 0->2 is wasted.
Replacing none on edge 0 turns on node 1 and all its downstream paths, a far bigger gain than replacing a live op.
Removing edge 2->3 hurts most when it carried the strongest op, a 3x3 conv.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the input->output edge with skip loses capacity, whereas replacing other ops with skip adds a helpful residual path.
Swapping a conv for parameter-free pooling on the final edge degrades accuracy much more than swapping any other op.
With edge 1->3 already absent, removing edge 0->3 leaves the output relying on a single path or disconnected entirely.
When edge 2->3 is absent, the output has fewer inputs, so a conv on the direct edge 0->3 contributes more.
Cutting edge 0 also disables the conv on edge 1->3, so the damage is larger when that conv is present.

- Node 1 is fed only by edge 0. If edge 0 is none, edges 2 and 4 carry nothing.
- Node 2 reaches the output only through edge 5.
- Removing paths into node 3 can disconnect the network, which collapses accuracy to about chance.
- Swapping out a 3x3 convolution costs much more than swapping out a weaker op.
